clinician.trajectory_summary: A 43-year-old male with 20-pack-year smoking history presented with a 5-month history of left second toe pain, numbness, tingling, and burning sensation. He was initially misdiagnosed with mild peripheral arterial disease (PAD) at an outside facility and underwent ingrown toenail resection. Following the procedure, he developed dry gangrene and non-healing wounds. Upon presentation to the vascular surgery clinic, comprehensive vascular workup was performed including pulse volume recordings (PVRs), ankle-brachial index (ABI), toe-brachial index (TBI), computed tomography angiography (CTA), and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI).
